cotton leaf curl virus.cause: Virus complex (begomoviruses) carried from plant to plant by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci
cotton leaf curl virus.symptoms: Veins on the underside of leaves become thickened and dark. Leaves curl up or down and cup, and small leaf-like outgrowths (enations) can appear under the veins. Plants may be stunted with fewer bolls. Symptoms show mostly on the upper young leaves.
look_alikes: Herbicide drift (2,4-D type damage can curl and twist leaves)
Heat or water stress, which can roll leaves
Sucking pests such as mites, thrips or jassids
cotton leaf curl virus.favourable_weather: Hot, dry weather that lets whitefly numbers build up. Whiteflies also survive on weeds and other crops between seasons.

weather_profile.note: This is a virus spread by an insect, so wet-weather risk does not apply in the same way. Do not use the fungal weather rating for this disease.

organic_control: Pull out and destroy plants with clear symptoms early, before whiteflies move the virus on
Remove weeds and alternate host plants in and around the field
Scout the underside of leaves for whiteflies regularly from early in the crop
Yellow sticky traps can help with monitoring whitefly numbers
cotton leaf curl virus.chemical_control: No spray can cure a plant that already has the virus. Sprays only target the whitefly, so product choice, rotation and timing must come from your agriculture officer or state university. No product or dose is given here.
prevention: Grow varieties or hybrids that your KVK or university recommends for your area
Keep whitefly numbers low early in the season, and monitor often
Avoid growing cotton next to other whitefly hosts such as okra, tomato, chilli and brinjal where possible
Keep field edges and bunds free of weeds
Avoid late sowing in areas where the disease is known
cotton leaf curl virus.when_to_call_expert: At the first plants with curling and thickened veins, and if many plants are affected, because it is reported mainly from north-west India and a new case in your area should be reported.

cotton alternaria leaf spot.cause: Fungi (mainly Alternaria species). Corynespora target spot looks very similar and can only be told apart by a lab.
cotton alternaria leaf spot.symptoms: Round to irregular brown spots with a ringed or target-like pattern, sometimes with a lighter centre and a yellow halo. Spots can join, and badly affected leaves yellow, curl and drop. It tends to show up on older leaves and when plants are stressed.
look_alikes: Bacterial blight (angular, water-soaked spots stopped by the veins)
Nutrient deficiency (potassium or magnesium) and leaf reddening
Heat and water stress, or sucking pests
cotton alternaria leaf spot.favourable_weather: Warm and humid weather with dew or rain, and plants under stress or short of potash. Dry, hot weather makes it less likely.

weather_profile.note: No verified numbers loaded yet. Add them from ICAR-CICR or JAU.

organic_control: Remove and destroy fallen and badly affected leaves where practical
Keep the crop well fed, because nutrient-starved plants get leaf spots worse
Avoid water stress and very dense, shaded crops
Control weeds so air moves through the crop
cotton alternaria leaf spot.chemical_control: Use only a product that is registered in India for cotton and this disease. Check the label or ask your agriculture officer for the product, dose and spray interval. No product or dose is given here.
prevention: Use seed and varieties recommended for your area
Plough in or remove crop residue after the season
Rotate with a non-host crop where practical
Follow your university fertiliser recommendation, including potash
cotton alternaria leaf spot.when_to_call_expert: If many plants are affected, if leaves are dropping heavily, or if the spots do not match the description, because nutrient problems and bacterial blight can look similar.

cotton bacterial blight.symptoms: Small, angular, water-soaked spots on leaves that are stopped by the veins and turn brown or black. Dark streaks can form along veins and stems (black arm), and bolls can get sunken dark spots and rot.
look_alikes: Alternaria or other fungal leaf spots (round, often ringed)
cotton bacterial blight.favourable_weather: Warm, humid weather with rain splash and wind-driven rain, which spreads the bacteria.

weather_profile.note: Warm, wet and windy weather. No verified numbers loaded yet.

organic_control: Remove and destroy badly affected plant parts and crop residue after the season
Avoid working in the field when plants are wet, so you do not spread the bacteria
Do not irrigate over the leaves
cotton bacterial blight.chemical_control: Use only a product that is registered in India for cotton and this disease. Bacterial diseases are not controlled by ordinary fungicides, so ask your agriculture officer for the correct product, dose and spray interval. No product or dose is given here.
prevention: Use healthy, treated seed from a trusted source
Use varieties recommended for your area
Rotate crops and clear residue, because the bacteria survive on crop debris and seed
cotton bacterial blight.when_to_call_expert: If angular spots, black streaks on stems or boll rot appear on many plants, because it can cause real yield loss.
